# Hardening notes — hogee run-4

Hunter hardening notes kept in ledger bookkeeping (not findings; no verdicts). Grouped by hunter.

**h-auth**

- packages/api/src/routes/demo-sale.ts: POST /api/demo/sale is any-persona (DEMO_MODE) and has no per-call limit. An anonymous local caller can fabricate Stripe test revenue (up to 99,999,999 minor per call), which the oracle key records on-chain and which opens RELEASE_STAGE exceptions labelled 'gate is met on-chain'. Consider requiring the officer persona, or tagging demo-originated sales so the officer's stage-release view and the stage-gate trace show the revenue as synthetic. Also cap the count to bound oracle gas.
- packages/api/src/routes/demo.ts reset: deletes every row of hogee_worker.halts, mock_payouts, noncanonical_watch and unresolved_watch regardless of deployment or scope, bypassing clearHalt's acknowledgement and open-safety-pause checks (apps/worker/src/store/halt.ts). It also continues when no anvilBaseline was recorded, wiping DB rows and halts while chain state remains. Refuse the reset when the baseline is missing or the revert fails, and clear halts through a clearHalt-equivalent path with a recorded note.
- packages/api/src/http/persona.ts AttemptLimiter: the officer-token limiter is one global window per process. Any local anonymous caller sending 5 wrong tokens per 15 min keeps officer minting locked even with the right token, and each attempt appends an ALERT trace (unbounded trace growth). Consider rate-limiting the trace writes and the attempts per client.
- packages/api/src/persona-cookie.ts: the cookie is stateless and host-only for 'localhost', which browsers do not isolate by port. Any other localhost:<port> server that the officer's browser requests under /api receives the officer cookie, and switching persona does not revoke an earlier officer value (up to 8h). Consider a server-side session id or epoch to revoke on persona switch, and a shorter officer TTL.
- packages/api-contract/src/routes.ts exportEvidence: POST /api/evidence/export has no persona list and is not demoOnly. It is a 501 stub today, but once task 1.16 implements it, any anonymous caller could trigger bundle builds. Choose its persona gate before implementing it.

**h-ext**

- Chat LLM spend has no per-caller or per-facility rate, concurrency or token budget. Each POST /api/chat (no cookie reads as founder) can drive up to PLANNER_MAX_STEPS=6 guarded calls with maxOutputTokens 4096 over up to 60 history turns. It is unreachable at dd824df only because the @hogee/privacy redact stub throws first (packages/api/src/routes/chat.ts:131). Add a per-process token bucket and a per-session turn cap before redaction once P3 redaction lands (builder item f).
- chat loadMessages reads the whole session history on every turn although only the last 60 turns are used (packages/api/src/services/chat-store.ts:24-31). Load only the last 60 rows by seq.
- startShortlist holds one pooled transaction client (pool max 8) across all fixture checks (packages/api/src/routes/suppliers.ts:22-43). Once P3 checks make network calls, a few concurrent anonymous shortlist requests can pin the API's DB pool. Run the checks outside the transaction.
- previewCountry stores a new preview plan_drafts row on every call with no cap (packages/api/src/routes/plans.ts:79), so plan_drafts grows linearly with anonymous calls.
- The inspection upload type check trusts the client-declared multipart part Content-Type (packages/api/src/routes/suppliers.ts:89). It is harmless today because only the keccak hash is kept and the file is never stored or served, but it must not be relied on if files are persisted.
- latestReadyShortlist picks the newest READY shortlist for the whole facility (packages/api/src/services/shortlist.ts:101-107). Any founder-persona caller can therefore supersede the founder's shortlist and its spec (quantity, so landed cost and milestone schedule) before SupplierApproval. This is bounded by the founder's signature over shortlistHash/scheduleHash and the finalize re-check, and is latent while the checks stubs throw.
- Agent memory is read for the whole facility across all chat sessions (packages/api/src/services/chat-store.ts:80-104). A slot answer given in any session, including one opened without a cookie, shapes later planner turns in every session. This is acceptable for a single founder only because PlanApproval needs the founder key.
- MEMORY_HMAC_KEY parsing treats any all-hex string as hex, and Buffer.from silently drops a trailing odd nibble (packages/api/src/runtime/env.ts:70). The 32-byte minimum still applies, so this is only a configuration footgun.

**h-money**

- packages/api/src/routes/exceptions.ts:73: the RELEASE_STAGE approval ignores the rowCount of its status-guarded UPDATE and always inserts Treasury.releaseStage, so a double or concurrent approve-and-deny produces extra lender-signed StageRelease attempts. The worker status check and the contract's st.released stop a second release; use decide() or check rowCount before insertAction.
- packages/api/src/services/policy-context.ts:161: the PolicyContext never sets ctx.loosens, so the core MAX_QUEUED_LOOSENS mirror check (loosen.ts:141) is dead off-chain. queueLoosen still enforces it on-chain.
- packages/api/src/services/exception-create.ts:38 and apps/worker/src/jobs/stage-gate.ts:57: the duplicate check on a pending RELEASE_STAGE for a stage and the insert are not atomic, so concurrent founder and worker creation can open two. A partial unique index on (facility_id, payload->>'stageId') where status in ('OPEN','APPROVED') would close this. The on-chain released flag already prevents a double release.
- packages/api/src/routes/facility.ts:103: fundFacility does not count in-flight Treasury.fund actions, and the worker fund builder (relay-calls.ts:167) binds the row to nothing. The chain caps funding at min(cap, plan total), so an extra row only reverts.
- packages/api/src/services/spend-proposal.ts:83: when several payees are payable on a pacing line, the API pays line.payeeIds[0], while the tick treats that case as ambiguous and skips. The payee is still listed and bound.
- packages/core/src/policy/loosen.ts:94 with policy-context.ts:104: isPlatformPayee reads only line bindings, so the line-less tax payee is refused off-chain as a WITHDRAW_RESERVE destination (functional bug), while line-bound platform payees (e.g. ads) are accepted. The contract allows any static platform payee.
- packages/api/src/routes/exceptions.ts:33 and proposals.ts:51: exceptions and escalations have no dedup or rate limit, and listExceptions returns only the newest 200 when no status filter is given. An anonymous founder persona can bury older pending or timelocked rows in the console's default view.
- packages/api/src/routes/exceptions.ts:108: veto accepts any persona (documented), so an anonymous caller can make the lender key cancel an officer- and founder-approved loosening. This is tighten-only; the gating belongs to the route-gate peer.

**h-ops**

- keys.ts scrub removes the signer keys only from the worker's own process.env. The parent shell and pnpm process environments, and the process's initial environment block (readable by same-user 'ps eww'), still hold them. XENDIT_SECRET_KEY is not scrubbed when PAYOUT_RAIL=mock, and DATABASE_URL stays in the env.
- Worker preflight (app.ts:92-149) never cross-checks Treasury.registry() against the manifest PlanRegistry, PlanRegistry.treasury() against the manifest Treasury, or the contracts' bytes32 deploymentId/chainTag against the manifest labels. All loop-* deployments share the LOOP key set (keys.ts:36-40), so a mis-paired manifest with the same lender and oracle keys passes preflight.
- checkObserver runs only when Treasury links an escrow (app.ts:100). A Treasury built from task-1.8 source with escrow 0 and an observer set skips the 'no worker key is the observer' check; the relayer is the only worker key the contracts do not keep off the observer.
- With CHAIN=local, LOCAL_RPC_URL accepts any http(s) host (env.ts:113-115), and preflight does not require chainId 31337. CHAIN=local plus DEPLOYMENT_FILE pointing at a Sepolia manifest therefore runs the signer over a single cleartext RPC, bypassing checkRpcUrl's https and two-provider rules (operator configuration only).
- The worker DEPLOYMENT_FILE path (app.ts:52-56) and the API DEPLOYMENT_FILE path (deployment.ts:76) check deploymentId but not chainTag, which feeds the EIP-712 salt. Manifest blockNumber, which seeds the orphan-watch cursor, is never checked against the chain.
- The facility-to-deployment binding uses labels only (deployment_id, chain_id). After an Anvil redeploy that reuses a label, old rows pass facilityDeploymentMismatch against the new contracts.
- Worker DDL uses CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS (schema.ts:17-124) and accepts pre-existing objects. If DB roles are ever separated, a role that pre-creates the hogee_worker schema would own the worker's safety tables.
- Demo reset (peer demo unit, officer + DEMO_MODE + chain 31337) deletes every hogee_worker.halts row globally and the worker keys' nonces rows (demo.ts:64-68). It still does so when no Anvil baseline exists, in which case the chain is not reverted (demo.ts:57). That clears an active halt without the ops resume checks and turns off outside-key-use detection until the next send.
- MEMORY_HMAC_KEY (env.ts:67-73) is checked for decoded length only. There is no entropy check like isStrongSecret, and Node's lenient base64 decoding accepts a low-entropy passphrase.

**h-relay**

- relay-calls.ts fund: the lender key signs Treasury.fund with request_json.amountMinor and no table binding. It relies on the officer-only API route and the on-chain ceiling (funded <= min(plan total, cap)); binding it to an officer-created record would close the gap for any other DB writer.
- relay-calls.ts recordDenied binds only proposal_hash to the denials row; lineId, decisionId and reasonCode come from request_json, so a different writer could aim circuit-breaker denials at any line. Bind them to the denial row's proposal_json and reason_code.
- relay-calls.ts builders look up the exception by request_json.exceptionId rather than chain_actions.ref_id, and never require the two to match (sync.ts landedTx keys on ref_id). Require request.exceptionId === row.refId.
- relay-calls.ts queueLoosen does not check the exception kind or that hashLoosenRequest(req) equals exceptions.loosen_id; adding both makes the lender co-signature bind to the exact loosening the officer saw.
- relay.ts selects every unsigned PENDING chain_actions row, including worker-internal rows (e.g. settle confirmSettlement, safety-pause) left by a failed sign. These are refused as an unknown kind with an ALERT trace; filter to API-created kinds.
- relay.ts reads the halt once per facility pass; agent-actions re-checks before every signature. A per-row assertNotHalted would match.
- relay-calls.ts releaseStage gate check uses block.timestamp > stage.deadline without the contract's deadline != 0 guard (TreasuryGovernance.sol:227), so a sales stage with deadline 0 would be refused (fail-closed divergence).
- Approved stage releases and officer-approved escalations refused on a transient revert are terminal, with no path to re-open the exception (stage-gate dedupes on APPROVED); this is a liveness issue only.
- sync.ts syncLoosens never re-reads CANCELLED exceptions, so a veto that loses the race with executeLoosen after executableAt leaves the DB CANCELLED while the chain says EXECUTED.

**h-settle**

- Lender-key external use is invisible during a halt. While halted, reconcile only inspects the lender, oracle and relayer nonces and alerts on holes, never on externalUse (reconcile.ts:117-121). report.nonces is not in the logged summary or the heartbeat (reconcile.ts:194-205), and app.ts discards the report. The safety pause's raiseNonce then raises the lender's next_nonce to the pending count (safety-pause.ts:142-145, 277), so after resume reconcileNonce never reports EXTERNAL_KEY_USE (halt-rules.ts:14-16) for a lender use made during the halt. Fix: run judgeNoncePass's EXTERNAL_KEY_USE alert (or record a halt reason) before raiseNonce for every role, and include nonces in the reconcile summary.
- Demo reset (peer-owned demo-routes unit) clears the worker kill switch without clearHalt. It deletes hogee_worker.halts outright (demo.ts:66-67), skipping the ack-through and open-pause refusals; the next reconcile closes open pause requests as HALT_CLEARED (safety-pause.ts:327-329). It also deletes the role nonces rows (demo.ts:64), so EXTERNAL_AGENT_KEY_USE detection is off until the allocator re-initialises from the chain's pending count (nonces.ts:63-73), which absorbs any prior external use. evm_revert does not undo a leaked key, and with no anvilBaseline nothing is reverted at all (demo.ts:57-60). Suggest resetting through clearHalt semantics, or refusing reset while an EXTERNAL_AGENT_KEY_USE or ORPHAN_SPEND reason is unacknowledged.
- With PAYOUT_RAIL=mock (the default, env.ts:149), the rail history settle trusts is the DB table hogee_worker.mock_payouts (mock-rail.ts:87-90, which also never compares amount, destination or reference). The API's DB principal already writes that schema (demo.ts:17, 66-67). So a DB writer can forge a SUCCEEDED or final FAILED attempt plus a matching payments mirror and get an oracle confirmSettlement or failSettlement sent (settle-decide.ts:99, 117-121), contrary to settle-decide.ts:5-15. No money moves on the mock rail and project.md:939 has the demo on xendit, but the guarantee should be scoped to XenditRail, or the mock table should be MACed or moved out of the API role's reach.
- The payout currency is taken from facilities.currency (settle.ts:67, 172). That value is neither on chain nor in the worker config: the chain is currency-agnostic and payoutAccountHash covers only channel, account number and holder (supplier.ts:79-81). A DB writer could change the currency, and so the real value, of a chain-bound minor amount. Pin it in the worker config (or the deployment manifest) and compare.
- decideSettlement only looks at the latest rail attempt when choosing fail or retry (settle-decide.ts:113-121). An earlier SUCCEEDED attempt does not stop failSettlement (which refunds the pocket) or a new attempt. This is unreachable with today's monotonic rail statuses; add `if (f.history.some(a => a.status === 'SUCCEEDED')) return blocked('PAYOUT_STATUS_MISMATCH')` before the fail and retry branches as defence in depth.
- A payout the rail refuses on every pass is retried forever, with no failSettlement, halt or watch; only an error log and an error heartbeat appear (settle.ts:258-264). Examples: an IDR amount with a fractional minor part (xendit-rail.ts:119), or a Xendit 4xx (xendit-rail.ts:330-337). The settlement stays open and its budget locked. Consider a consecutive-pass watch like unresolved_watch.

**h-sign**

- LoosenRequest display (packages/api/src/services/signing/loosen-request.ts:36-40 with titleOf in packages/api/src/services/exceptions.ts:128) omits newValue for EXTEND_EXPIRY: the founder signs 'Extend the agent's authority' or 'Extend the X pocket's end date' without seeing the new date (bounded to now + 90 days by core loosen rules, the timelock and officer approval). Add a row with the new expiry from loosenFields.newValue.
- LoosenRequest 'Most money this change can move' shows the creation-time exceptions.blast_radius_minor instead of a value recomputed at prepare time; recompute it with blastRadiusOf against the current policy world.
- verifyPasskeyAssertion/passkeyContextProblem (packages/api/src/routes/signatures.ts:110-122) do not reject clientData.crossOrigin === true, though registration does (webauthn.ts:102); frame-ancestors 'none' mitigates it today. Add the same check (and refuse a topOrigin) for parity.
- SupplierApproval shows 'Pays out to' from suppliers.record_json.xenditTest but signs candidate.payoutAccountHash from the shortlist without asserting payoutAccountHash(account) === candidate.payoutAccountHash (supplier-approval.ts:79-98). The two are consistent today because both come from the same catalog fixture; assert it in planOrder. Order quantity (an input to quoteHash) is not displayed, and the newest READY shortlist can be replaced by any persona before the request.
- MilestoneRelease shows only the raw evidenceHash, and the inspection upload (packages/api/src/routes/suppliers.ts:87-104) is founder-persona and overwrites evidence_hash until release. A change after the request fails closed at finalize, but one before the request is signed as shown; consider binding the upload to the founder key or refusing overwrite once set.
- parseAuthData (packages/api/src/services/signing/webauthn.ts:146) decodes the COSE key non-exactly and accepts trailing bytes even when the ED (0x80) flag is clear; require exact decoding unless ED is set.
- The officer approval reviews {credentialId, qx, qy}, but registerFounderKey also sets ownerEOA from FOUNDER_WALLET_ADDRESS config (packages/api/src/routes/facility.ts:63-68, passkey.ts:105). It is operator-trusted and re-checked by the worker (apps/worker/src/jobs/relay-calls.ts:156), but the officer never sees it; include ownerEOA in the reviewed tuple.
